dimensions.rationale: Playfair italic standfirsts add an FT-standfirst editorial layer beneath each section title — reinforces private-bank typography hierarchy without crowding the page.
Standfirst gives the reader a one-line orienting answer per section before diving into KPIs and prose. The 'so what' is no longer trapped in the AI block.
No change to engine, math, or AI prompt rigor in this pass.
Already a strength; Sprint A/B/C is consolidation, not new positioning.
Per-section narration unchanged; cross-section synthesis still missing (Sprint D).

Section titles re-framed from topical nouns ('Stratégie fiscale', 'Immobilier') to decision-framed nouns ('Marges d'efficacité fiscale', 'Place de l'immobilier'). Decision-flow now legible from the TOC alone. Biggest single-pass IA win — but section reorder within chapters not done; remaining gap is sequence ('priorities first') vs current thematic grouping.
No advisor-mode work — deferred (B2B distraction at consumer stage).
All new copy (labels + standfirsts) is observational, present-tense facts + conditional projections. AMF-clean by construction. No FORBIDDEN verbs introduced.

Real moves on emotional engagement need life-event visualizations + recovery-arc framing in low-grade narration (qa-check flagged: missing_recovery_path in 6 profiles).
Sec(sub) + KPI(tier) are clean extensions, backward-compatible. No new scaling lever, no friction added.

strengths: Chapter titles success-tinted correctly ('Pourquoi cette transition tient' — confident posture matches A-)
Decision-framed section labels appear in TOC ('Trajectoire patrimoniale', 'Marges d'efficacité fiscale', 'Transmission successorale')
Standfirsts read as orienting subtitles, not redundant with section content
AMF tone preserved throughout (observational, conditional projections)
weaknesses: Section order within Chapter III still thematic — priorites_action / leviers should precede tax/decum/succession sub-levers per audit's decision-flow recommendation
KPIs in Sommaire exécutif still all equal visual weight — no hero KPI signal of 'the one that answers the chapter question'

Cross-section linkage absent: meltdown insight references 'fenêtre 63-72', tax insight names lifetime-tax savings of $8K — but no synthesis paragraph naming the meltdown→tax→estate axis as ONE planning problem
'estate transfer to second spouse' tension (the codex audit named this as the archetype tension for HNW couples) is implicit, not surfaced as a thread across chapters

strengths: Chapter title for F-grade reads correctly as architecture/diagnostic, not glowing ('Architecture de votre plan' rather than 'Pourquoi ça tient')
Standfirst on debt section is sharp: 'Le coût mathématique des dettes actuelles sur la trajectoire patrimoniale.' — names the framing without judging
AMF compliance held even at 6% — narration does not shame, does not catastrophize
weaknesses: qa-check flagged missing_recovery_path: at 6% the report must structure a numbered phase plan (stabilize → deleverage → rebuild → re-plan per archetype prompt rule). Current narration diagnoses but doesn't sequence the recovery arc.

Standfirsts are GENERIC (not parameterized with this profile's specific numbers — same standfirst would render for any debt_young persona). Real names + amounts would land harder for a high-anxiety reader.

No emotional opening — audit's P0 ('reduce anxiety, not optimization') most relevant here. The reader sees F + 6% and the report's opening should explicitly NAME what's in their control before naming risks.
Cross-section: debt-vs-savings race (the archetype tension) is described in the debt section but not connected upstream to savings_analysis or downstream to projection.

strengths: Chapter title 'Architecture of your plan + corporation' correctly signals the CCPC structural lens
Corporate-strategy standfirst 'Salary, dividend, or deferral — how money leaves the corporation' is exactly the decision question the section answers
EN typography hierarchy matches FR — bilingual parity preserved
Chapter III chapter title 'Corporate & tax strategy' bundles the right concepts (audit recommended this combined framing)
weaknesses: Order of decisions in CCPC section: per prompt rule it should be 'corporate extraction → tax integration → personal RRSP/TFSA → public benefits'. The section sequence in the TOC keeps thematic grouping (corp+remuneration sub-section), not the decision pipeline.
RDTOH / GRIP / capital-dividend-account nuance not surfaced in standfirst — these are the case-driver knobs for a CCPC owner.
Cross-section: corporation → personal extraction → tax → estate is one continuous problem; current report renders them as 4 separate sections.

summary: Sprint A+B+C IA refactor on the realai pipeline closes the audit's IA gap (7.8 → 8.5 estimated) and the Key-Takeaway gap (was missing, now present). Net +1.5 points (87 → 88.5). Remaining audit deltas live in: (1) per-section KPI hero tagging — quick win, ~3-4h work; (2) per-profile parameterized standfirsts using real numbers — quick win once a generator is wired; (3) Sprint D cross-section synthesis — the biggest lever, ~10-14 days; (4) sensitivity narrative slot — small targeted prompt+renderer addition; (5) recovery-arc enforcement in low-grade reports — content/prompt work, not structural. The architecture is in place; everything below is content sharpening.
